records.claimQuote: Clients upload a photo directly to object storage
records.rationale: 'Short-lived' is a real validity bound on the upload URL (set reading), but it is also defensibly an adjective describing the mechanism, a limit too minor to matter (not_a_condition reading). The source gives no further weight either way; R1 itself marked it low confidence.

records.conditionQuote: applies a rate limit of 120 requests per minute per account
records.claimQuote: The gateway terminates TLS, checks the caller's access token with the auth service, applies a rate limit
records.rationale: A numeric bound on gateway traffic; the gateway's role stays true without the value.

records.conditionQuote: If the auth service cannot be reached, the gateway rejects the request instead of letting it through unchecked.
records.claimQuote: checks the caller's access token with the auth service, applies a rate limit of 120 requests per minute per account, and routes the request to the right service
records.rationale: u9 states check-then-route unconditionally; when the auth service is unreachable the check cannot happen and the request is not routed but rejected, so u9 is false for that case and silent on fail-open vs fail-closed. R1 reads it so (golden links it to u8+u9 without a binding); R2's set reading treats it as an added property but the 'instead of letting it through' wording marks a case where u9's routing does not occur.

records.conditionQuote: Photo bytes are served to clients by the CDN, never by the gateway.
records.claimQuote: Every client request enters through the API gateway.
records.rationale: Photo byte loads bypass the gateway, so 'every client request' is misleading without the exception.

records.conditionQuote: followers who have notifications turned on
records.claimQuote: asks the push-notification provider to alert followers
records.rationale: Without the scope the alert claim (and the u32 flow step) reads as alerting all followers, which is false for followers with notifications off.

records.conditionQuote: The queue keeps an event for up to 7 days
records.claimQuote: a worker outage delays thumbnails but does not lose uploads
records.rationale: 'Does not lose uploads' is false for an outage longer than the 7-day retention.

records.conditionQuote: A photo whose processing keeps failing stays in the "processing" state and is not shown in any feed.
records.claimQuote: A media processing worker picks up the event, creates the thumbnails and marks the photo "ready".
records.rationale: Claim reading (R1; golden links it to the worker claims without a binding): the worker/flow steps state unconditionally that the photo is marked ready and reaches feeds, false for a photo whose processing keeps failing. Set reading (R2): the flow section describes the success path, which stays true, and the failure path is a separate caveat. The source presents the flow as the main path without saying whether it is meant as guaranteed, so it does not settle this.

records.claimQuote: keeps ready-made feed pages in the cache
records.rationale: Cache lifetime bound; caching feed pages stays true without it.

records.conditionQuote: Pinhole only sends it requests and does not control when an alert arrives
records.claimQuote: asks the push-notification provider to alert followers who have notifications turned on
records.rationale: Delivery-timing caveat; the 'asks the provider' claim stays true.

records.conditionQuote: The cost is that a new photo takes a few seconds to appear in feeds.
records.claimQuote: the upload service and the workers only meet through the message queue
records.rationale: The stated trade-off of the queue decision; the decision stays true.

records.conditionQuote: Originals can be up to 25 MB
records.claimQuote: clients send bytes straight to object storage and the upload service only signs the URL and records the result
records.rationale: Size bound and deciding fact; the direct-upload decision stays true without it.

records.conditionQuote: we accept that their outages are outside our control
records.claimQuote: We use a third-party CDN and push-notification provider instead of running our own
records.rationale: Accepted risk of the buy decision; the decision stays true.

records.conditionQuote: How failed processing is retried, and when a stuck photo is cleaned up, is not decided yet.
records.claimQuote: A photo whose processing keeps failing stays in the "processing" state and is not shown in any feed.
records.rationale: Open question on the failure path; the stated stuck-state behaviour holds for now.

records.conditionQuote: The design is sized for about 2 million daily active users at launch.
records.claimQuote: Pinhole lets people post photos and see the photos of the accounts they follow in a feed.
records.rationale: A real capacity scope of the whole design, but it limits no particular claim sentence (u1 is a feature statement that stays true at any scale), so the claim it limits cannot be pinned down; R1 treated it as scope description, R2 as a set condition.

readings.note: implicit: R1 notes call u40 'an open question with no limited claim'

records.conditionQuote: Whether the feed service should precompute feeds for accounts with very many followers is left to the feed service's own low-level design.
records.claimQuote: The feed service builds each person's feed from the photos of the accounts they follow
records.rationale: The open question is explicitly about how the feed service builds feeds (u14) for high-follower accounts, so there is a claim it qualifies; u14 stays true, so it is a set caveat, parallel to the agreed open-question record c13.
